ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Clinical pharmacology foundations: 3

An oral dose undergoes incomplete absorption and first-pass metabolism, so only part reaches the bloodstream unchanged. Which pharmacokinetic measure describes this fraction rather than the speed at which the drug is later eliminated?

  1. Pharmacokinetics
  2. Pharmacodynamics
  3. Clearance
  4. Therapeutic window
  5. Bioavailability
Answer and explanation

Bioavailability

Bioavailability is the fraction of an administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged.

Option explanations

Bioavailability: Bioavailability is the fraction of an administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged.

Pharmacokinetics: Pharmacokinetics describes absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination and their effects on drug concentration. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Pharmacodynamics: Pharmacodynamics relates drug concentration and target interaction to biological effects. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Clearance: Clearance expresses the volume of plasma effectively cleared of drug per unit time. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Therapeutic window: The therapeutic window separates exposures associated with benefit from those causing unacceptable toxicity. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
